resolution.note:
Official skill: herdrdev/herdr skills/herdr/SKILL.md, https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/blob/master/skills/herdr/SKILL.md (linked from the herdr.dev docs index https://herdr.dev/llms.txt, "Agent skill file"; `herdr --skill` prints the copy bundled with the binary). Compared at v0.9.5, the stable release on herdr.dev: tag commit 2ecf19a92fc3a7fff75b6ce3655ef04f4625ec01, file blob 4943e5575e941a7820ea01ca9416e79749c3ddc3. Installed herdr 0.9.1 bundles blob bcb22ba8d7b8259f25fa2bfd76dd5e520fd52fbc, byte-identical to the local ~/.claude/skills/herdr/SKILL.md; 0.9.1 to 0.9.5 changes prose only, none of the commands below.
Verdicts (successor-launch.ts job: official command: verdict):
1 server up: `herdr status`: already same; text parse kept, `status --json` is in 0.9.1 --help but in neither the CLI reference nor the skill.
2 caller workspace and tab: `pane get <id>` (CLI reference) or `pane current --current` (skill): already same; the server resolves both with parse_pane_id (alias-aware) and live replies carry the identical pane object; keep the explicit id, it never falls back to the focused pane.
3 create tab: `tab create --workspace --cwd --label --env --no-focus`, ids from .result.tab.tab_id and .result.root_pane.pane_id: already same; keep a tab, not the skill's default sibling pane, because the operator asked for tabs (2026-10-30, t-gnydgbs).
4 start the agent: `pane run <pane> <command>` versus `agent start <name> --kind K --pane P -- args`: keep ours; agent start rejects any argument holding a control character (a newline or tab in the prompt), needs a unique [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31} name while ours is free text, runs Herdr's canonical executable so the KRN_SUCCESSOR_AGENT override is lost, returns agent_not_ready on a startup dialog although the agent is live, and its reply cannot be captured without creating a pane (KRN-12).
5 read agent state: `agent get <pane>`: same command; ADOPTED the documented error channel: Herdr prints errors as JSON on stderr with exit 1 and we read stdout only, so a vanished pane was never recognised (--retire polled the full 180 s, the ledger kept dead records); fixed, red at base.
6 wait for the predecessor: `agent wait <pane> --until idle --until done --timeout MS`: ADOPTED in --retire in place of the 5 s sleep loop; agent get still verifies agent and session before the close and any wait failure falls back to a bounded pause.
7 rename, list, close: `tab rename`, `tab list --workspace`, `pane close`, `tab close`: already same; closing panes we did not create is operator-requested (t-w5gnqye) and guarded by agent, session, status and workspace checks.
8 read output: none used by ours (`pane read`, `pane wait-output`).
Left open: (a) the skill requires HERDR_ENV=1 and forbids controlling the focused Herdr session from outside Herdr; with no HERDR_PANE_ID but a running server the launcher still creates a tab in the active workspace; operator decision, unchanged. (b) the skill says `pane run` success is admission, not start; the launcher reports success on exit 0; t-p4akh87.
Evidence: read-only captures from herdr 0.9.1 (agent get, agent wait match, timeout and agent_not_found, pane get, pane current, tab list, status) back the tests in test/fixtures/herdr; the exact `agent wait` argv ran against the live server. No mutating herdr command was run.

title: Compare successor launch with the official herdr skill
body:
Outcome: the krn-handoff successor launch (scripts/claude/successor-launch.ts, memory herdr-handoff-tabs) is compared with the official herdr skill published by the herdr project, and KRN adopts its documented commands wherever they cover the same job.
Operator, verbatim (2026-11-01): "czy sprawdzlaes oficjalny herdr skill z ich serwisu? sprawdz to potem"
Proof: a recon verdict file naming the official skill source URL and version, a command-by-command comparison with successor-launch.ts, and either a PR that adopts the official commands or a recorded reason per difference.
